Highlights
A phenolic glycoside from Moringa oleifera Lam. can ameliorate metabolic syndrome 
in db/db mice
Niazirin effectively regulated energy homeostasis
Niazirin improved hepatic carbohydrate metabolism in db/db mice through AMPK 
pathway


2
Niazirin reduce fatty acid synthesis and induce fatty acid oxidation in db/db mice 
through AMPK pathway
Abstract
The increasing incidence of metabolic syndrome requires more functional food 
products with low cost and excellent effects to assist treatment. The crude extract of 
Moringa oleifera Lam. showed excellent hypoglycemic activity. The current study 
was designed to investigate the effects and mechanism of niazirin, a bioactive 
component from Moringa oleifera Lam. seed, on diabetic metabolic syndrome. 
C57BL/6J mice were treated daily with 5 mL/kg/body weight (BW) of saline, while 
db/db mice were similarly treated with 5 mL/kg/BW of saline, 10 and 20 mg/kg/BW 
of niazirin, respectively. Results indicated that niazirin could significantly reduce 
body weight, water and food intake, improve hyperglycemia, insulin resistance, 
inflammation, carbohydrate and lipid metabolism, non-alcoholic fatty liver. 
Furthermore, niazirin improved the hepatic energy metabolism via AMPK signaling 
pathway. Our study provides an evidence of an edible plant product, niazirin, may 
help in the treatment of metabolic syndrome.
Keywords: Moringa oleifera Lam.; diabetes; AMPK; metabolic syndrome; lipids 
metabolism; carbohydrate metabolism
Abbreviations
Adenosine 
5’-monophosphate 
(AMP)-activated 
protein 
kinase 
(AMPK); 
Peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor alpha (PPARα); Sterol regulatory 


3
element-binding protein (SREBP-1); Fatty acid synthase (FAS); Acetyl-CoA 
carboxylase (ACC); Sirtuin 1 (SirT1); Peroxisome proliferator activated receptor-1α 
(PGC-1α); Forkhead box protein O1 (FOXO1); Hepatocyte nuclear factor 4 alpha 
(HNF-4α); Phosphofructo-2-kinase/fructose-2,6-bisphosphatase-3 (PFKFB3).
1. Introduction
Metabolic syndrome is a group of clinical syndromes with hypertension, central 
obesity, diabetes, hyperlipidemia and abnormal glucose metabolism (Alberti, Zimmet, 
Shaw, & Grundy, 2006)et al., The dramatic increase in metabolic syndrome can be 
attributed tocaused by the modern lifestyle which created an imbalance between 
energy intake and energy expenditure (Sharabi, Lin, Tavares, Dominy, Camporez, 
Perry, et al., 2017). Natural products have always been the good option for patients 
with metabolic diseases to assist conventional treatment due to its low treatment costs 
and side effects. Hence, it is necessary to find new phytochemicals extracted from 
normal food that can ameliorate metabolic syndrome.
Moringa oleifera Lam. is widely distributed in the tropical and subtropical regions. 
It is an edible plant with great nutritional value, which is rich in protein, vitamins, 
mineral elements and other nutrients (Falowo, Mukumbo, Idamokoro, Lorenzo, 
Afolayan, & Muchenjeet al., 2018). Different parts of Moringa oleifera Lam. can be 
cooked in different ways and eaten as vegetables or dietary supplementary. In 
addition, as a kind of high-quality edible raw material for improving metabolic 
disorder, Moringa oleifera Lam. attracts more and more researcher’s’ attention. It has 
been demonstrated that Moringa oleifera Lam. has therapeutic effects of diabetes, and 
can ameliorate the abnormal carbohydrates and lipid metabolism of diabetic patients 
as well as alleviate metabolic syndrome (Direk Aekthammarat, et al., 2019; 


4
Omodanisi, Aboua, & Oguntibejuet al., 2017). Studies have also shown that adding a 
certain amount of Moringa oleifera Lam. to the daily diet of diabetic patients can 
significantly reduce their blood glucose and glycosylated hemoglobin levels (Mbikay, 
2012). However, most studies focus on the activity of Moringa oleifera Lam. extract. 
The specific active components of Moringa oleifera Lam. for and mechanism on the 
improvinge metabolic syndrome and their mechanismsactivity of Moringa oleifera 
Lam. have not been determined. In our previous research, a component named 
niazirin was isolated from Moringa oleifera Lam. which can significantly improve 
glucose-induced oxidative stress (Wang, Bao, Shen, Zengin, Lyu, Xiao, & Wenget al., 
2019). In the present study, we explored the function and mechanism of niazirin on 
metabolic syndrome based on db/db mice. The chemical structure of niazirin was 
shown in Figure 1.
AMPK is a sensor of the AMP/ATP or ADP/ATP ratio thus can be used to measure 
cellular energy levels, it regulates cellular energy homeostasis by regulating 
carbohydrate and lipid metabolism (Angin, Beauloye, Horman, & Bertrandet al., 
2016; D Grahame, Ross, & Hawleyet al., 2012; Fazakerley, Holman, Anna, James, 
Jacqueline, & Costeret al., 2010). Activation of AMPK enhances tissue sensitivity to 
insulin, glucose uptake, and fatty acid oxidation, and reduces inhibits gluconeogenesis, 
cholesterol, and triglyceride production, playsing an important role in regulating 
energy metabolism. In this regard, finding some phytochemical from food materials to 
activate AMPK is a sensible strategy in the treatment of metabolic syndrome.
The present study was the first time to examine if niazirin could regulate the 
hepatic lipid and glucose metabolism thus ameliorate metabolic syndrome in vivo. We 
also attempted to assure the exact mechanism of niazirin on energy metabolism. The 


5
major findings of this study were that niazirin reduced lipid accumulation, increased 
lipid oxidation, reduced gluconeogenesis and whlie increased glycolysis in liver, and 
AMPK was critical for these observed effects.
2. Materials and methods
2.1 Niazirin preparation
Seeds of Moringa oleifera Lam. were collected in October 2015 in Nansha Town, 
Yuanyang County, Yunnan Province, China. A voucher sample (No. 20151020) was 
preserved in Nanjing University of Chinese Medicine and identified by Prof. Qi-Nan 
Wu. Moringa Oleifera seeds were extracted by boiling water twice and the crude 
fractions were extracted by macroporous resin column. The concentrated fraction was 
obtained by silica gel chromatography. Finally, niazirin was prepared by medium 
pressure liquid chromatography with ODS column as chromatographic column from 
the cencentreted fracion. The purtiy is determined ≥95% (Wang, et al., 2019).
2.21 Animal experiments
A total of 18 male db/db mice C57BL/6J and 6 C57BL/6J wild-type mice db/db 
mice were purchased form the Laboratory Animal Center in Nanjing University of 
Chinese Medicine at 5 weeks of age, the ethics number is SCXK2016-0010. The 
study was conducted under strict guidelines of Animal Care Committee of Nanjing 
University of Chinese Medicine. Animals were housed in the constant temperature 
environment (25°C and 50±5% humidity) in 12 h light/12 h dark circle. All mice have 
free access to food (standard chow diet) and water. After 2 weeks adaptive feed, db/db 
mice were divided into 3 groups randomly (n=6) and treated daily via gavage with 
vehicle (saline, 5 mL/kg/day, DM group), niazirin (10 mg/kg/day, 20 mg/kg/day, 


6
DM+10 and DM+20 group). 6 wild-type mice were treated with saline as normal 
control (WT group). The wWeight, food intake, water intake and blood glucose level 
were recorded during the study. After 4 weeks of administration, the mice were fasted 
overnight, and the blood samples were collected from the orbital vein. The liver was 
removed and weighed then frozen at -80° C for estimation of biochemical parameters. 
Mice were sacrificed with sodium pentobarbital according to Animal Care Committee 
of Nanjing University of Chinese Medicine standard guidelines. 
2.32 Oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT)
On the third week, OGTT was performed after more than 12 h of fasting. After the 
measurement of baseline blood glucose (0 min), the mice were given 2 g/kg glucose 
orally, and the blood glucose was measured at 30 min, 60 min, 90 min and 120 min, 
respectively.
2.43 Plasma insulin and HOMA-IR
After 4 weeks of administration, blood samples were collected after overnight 
fasting and centrifuged at 3000 rpm for 15 min. Plasma insulin was determined by 
Elisa kit (Nanjing Jiancheng Bioengineering Institute, China). Insulin sensitivity was 
also calculated from HOMA-IR (insulin resistance homeostasis model assessment) 
according to the following formula (Matthews et al., 1985): HOMA-IR = (fasting 
blood glucose (mmol/L)] × [fasting insulin (mIU/L)] / 22.5 (Matthews, Hosker, 
Rudenski, Naylor, Treacher, & Turner, 1985).
2.54 Estimation of biochemical parameters in plasma and liver 


7
Plasma TNF-α, IL-10, LDL, HDL, TC, TG, NEFA levels were estimated by assay 
kits (Nanjing Jiancheng Bioengineering Institute, China). Glycogen content and 
activities of glucose metabolic enzymes in liver were measured by assay kits (Nanjing 
Jiancheng Bioengineering Institute, China)
2.65 Histological analysis
The liver dissection of mice was fixed with 10% formaldehyde and paraffin 
embedded. 
Tissue 
sections 
were 
observed 
and 
photographed 
under 
haematoxylin-eosin staining (H&E) (Nikon Eclipse E100 microscope; Nikon, Tokyo, 
Japan).
2.76 Western blots
Tissue fractions from mice were weighed and RIPA and PMSF (Beyotime, China) 
mix (99:1) were added in at the ratio of 1:10. Lysis was initiated in a tissue grinding 
mill. After centrifugation at 13,000 rpm for 20 min, the supernatant was transferred to 
new centrifuge tubes. Protein concentration was determined by BCA method. Add 
calculated amount 5× loading buffer into protein sample to make the final 1× loading 
buffer. After brief centrifuge and vortex, the samples were separated by 10% 
SDS-PAGE gels and transferred to nitrocellulose membranes. The membranes were 
blocked in 5% milk for at least 1 hour and incubated at 4°C overnight with the 
following primary antibodies. Antibodies against AMPK, p-AMPK (THR172), FAS, 
p-ACC (Ser79), ACC were obtained from Cell Signaling Technology and used at a 
dilution of 1:1000; antibodies against SREBP-1 and PPARα were obtained from 
Abcam and were used at a dilution of 1:500; antibodies against p-ACC (Ser79), 
SirT1, FOXO1 were obtained from Beyotime Technology and were used at a dilution 


8
of 1:500; antibodies against HNF-4α, PGC-1α, PFKFB-3 were obtained from Solarbio 
and were used at a dilution of 1:200. Then, these membranes were washed 4 times for 
15 min with TBST buffer and incubated secondary antibodies (Cell Signaling 
Technology, USA) for 1 h at room temperature. After washed 4 times for 15 min 
again, membranes were incubated in ECL substrate at least 30 seconds to observe the 
protein bands. Western blots were quantified by Image J.
2.87 Statistical analysis 
All data are expressed as the mean ± SD of the three independent experiments as 
indicated. The level of statistical significance was determined by analysis of variance 
(ANOVA). Tukey’s multiple comparison test was performed for multiple 
comparisons among all groups if overall p < 0.05. A probability (p value) of < 0.05 
was considered statistically significant.
3 Results
3.1 Niazirin decreased body weight, food and water intake of db/db mice
To investigate the effect of niazirin on the basic physiological indexes of mice, we 
recorded the data of body weight, food intake and water intake of animals over 4 
weeks. The weight of db/db mice in the model group was significantly higher than 
WT mice (p < 0.01), after niazirin treatment, the weight of db/db mice increased more 
slowly than DM group, which was a dose-dependent difference (Figure 2A). The 
average daily food intake of db/db mice is significantly higher than WT mice, after 
the treatment of niazirin, food intake of db/db mice were reduced (Figure 2B). As 
shown in Figure 2C, the water intake of db/db mice is almost twice as the 
wild-typeWT mice with the progress of diabetic conditions. At the beginning of 
administration, the water intake of DM+10 and DM+20 mice even showed a trend of 


9
increase compared with DM mice, however, at the end of administration, the decrease 
of water intake of DM+10 and DM+20 were observed. These facts suggest that 
niazirin hasve an optimistic effect on physiological indexes in db/db mice.
3.2 Niazirin improved hyperglycemia and inflammation in db/db mice
After 6 h fasting, FBG (Fasting blood glucose) was determined by caudal vein 
blood sample. As shown in Figure 2D, during the 4-week observation, the FBG of 
db/db mice continued to increase compared with the wild-type controlWT group (p < 
0.01). At the beginning, the FBG of DM+10 and DM+20 mice are higher than DM 
mice, after 4 weeks of niazirin treatedtreatment, the FBG of db/db mice showed a 
fluctuant decreased trend. In the fourth week of administration, the FBG of db/db 
mice decreased significantly. It suggested that niazirin have a statistically significant 
effect on maintain blood glucose within a normal range. 
Increased or decreased contents of cytokines would make metabolic syndrome 
more susceptible; TNF-α (Tumor Necrosis Factor-α) is a proinflammatory cytokine 
induces injury and infection and which plays a key role in metabolic syndrome, 
including obesity-induced insulin resistance (Moller, 2000). Anti-inflammatory 
cytokines IL-10 (Interleukin-10) can inhibit the migration and proliferation of 
inflammatory cells by reducing the release of factors and inflammatory mediators, and 
low serum IL-10 levels are associated with an increased risk of metabolic syndrome 
(Forte, Pilato, Vaccarino, Sanacore, Candore, Romano, et al., 2010). The level of 
plasma TNF-α in db/db mice was significantly higher than wild-typeWT group (p < 
0.01) (Figure 2E). Both dose of niazirin dramatically reduce TNF-α in db/db mice (p 
< 0.01). Compared with the wild-type controlWT group, a notable decrease in IL-10 
level was observed in db/db mice (p < 0.01), and niazirin increased plasma IL-10 in a 


10
dose-dependence manner with a significant difference (Figure 2F). These results 
indicate that niazirin could improve hyperglycemia and inflammation in db/db mice.
3.3 Niazirin ameliorated insulin resistance in db/db mice
OGTT, fasting plasma insulin, HOMA-IR were measured to assess insulin 
resistance (Figure 2H to J). Compared with the wild-type miceWT group, the blood 
glucose level of db/db miceDM group increased sharply significantly after glucose 
treatment, while mice treated with niazirin showed significant improvement compared 
with the DM group and showed a certain dose dependence. The fasting plasma insulin 
and HOMA-IR of db/db miceDM group were significantly increased (p < 0.01) 
compared with WT group. Both doses of niazirin significantly reduced plasma insulin 
levels and HOMA-IR (p < 0.01) compared with DM group. These results suggested 
that niazirin improved insulin resistance and increased insulin sensitivity in db/db 
mice.
3.4 Niazirin reduced gluconeogenesis and induced glycolysis in liver of db/db mice
Based on the hypoglycemic activity of niazirin, we determined the effects of 
niazirin on hepatic carbohydrate metabolism since liver play a key role in 
carbohydrate metabolism of body. Hepatic glycogen and key enzymes in liver glucose 
metabolism, including HK (hexokinase) and PK (pyruvate kinase), G6Pase 
(glucose-6-phosphatase) and PEPCK (phosphoenolpyruvate carboxykinase) were 
estimated by ELISA kits, which are key rate-limiting enzymes in glycolytic and 
gluconeogenic pathway, respectively (Figure 3). Compared with the wild-type 
controlWT group, the glycogen content in the liver of db/db mice was significantly 
reduced, reflecting that the ability to synthesize hepatic glycogen of db/db mice was 


11
impaired. The treatment of niazirin dramatically increased the content of hepatic 
glycogen in db/db mice, thus restoring the impaired synthesis of hepatic glycogen in 
db/db mice (Figure 3A). The activity of HK and PK, two glycolytic enzymes in the 
liver, was significantly damaged reduced in db/db mice compared with normal 
miceWT group., Hhowever, administration of niazirin increased activity of glycolytic 
enzymes with a significant difference, demonstrating that catabolic rate of glucose in 
the liver of db/db mice was repaired (Figure 3B to C). The activity of G6Pase and 
PEPCK in the liver of db/db mice was abnormally higher than wild-typeWT group. 
The treatment of niazirin inhibited the abnormally high activity of these two 
gluconeogenic enzymes (Figure 3D to E). These results illustrated that glucose uptake 
and utilization are dramatically decreased inhibited in db/db mice with metabolic 
syndrome, niazirin treatment can could improve activity of PK and HK activity, 
reduce G6Pase and PEPCK activity in the liver of db/db mice and thus increase 
glycogen storage in the liver.
3.5 The mechanisms of niazirin improved hepatic carbohydrate metabolism in db/db 
mice
  To further investigate the mechanism by niazirin exerted its hepatic carbohydrate 
metabolism regulatory activity, we measured the expression of glucose 
metabolism-related proteins, such as SirT1, PGC-1α, HNF-4α and FOXO1. AMPK 
enhance the activity of SirT1, resulting in the deacetylation and activation of PGC-1α 
(Carles, et al., 2009). PGC-1α promotes hepatic gluconeogenesis by coactivating 
HNF-4α and FOXO1, which are essential for the transcription of gluconeogenic gene 
Pck1 and G6pc, thus control the expression of gluconeogenic enzymes PEPCK and 
G6Pase (Sharabi, et al., 2017). Compared with the DM group, we found that niazirin 


12
effectively increased the level of SirT1 in db/db mice (Figure 4A). The expression of 
PGC-1α, HNF-4α and FOXO1 in the liver are highly elevated in db/db mice, but the 
treatment with niazirin inactivated these proteins (Figure 4A to B). Taken together, 
these results suggested that niazirin regulates gluconeogenesis by altering levels of 
SirT1, PGC-1α, HNF-4α and FOXO1 in liver.
  Moreover, PFKFB3 activated by AMPK phosphorylation can could stimulate 
glycolysis by produce fructose-2, 6-diphosphate, an allosteric activator of glycolysis 
phosphofructoskinase-1 (Anne-Sophie, Caroline, Luc, & Louiset al., 2002). We found 
that niazirin effectively stimulated the phosphorylation of AMPK (Figure 6A), thus 
increased the expression of PFKFB3 (Figure 4C), indicating that niazirin might 
improve glycolysis via the activation of AMPK/PFKFB3 pathway.
3.6 Niazirin ameliorated plasma lipids profiles in db/db mice  
To test the effects of niazirin oin ameliorating metabolic syndrome by improving 
lipid metabolism disorder, plasma lipid profiles including LDL-C (Low-Density 
Lipoprotein Cholesterol), HDL-C (High-Density Lipoprotein Cholesterol),  TC 
(Total Cholesterol), TG (Triglyceride) and NEFA (Non-esterified Fatty Acids) were 
measured (Figure 5C to G). Levels of LDL-C, TC, TG and NEFA in db/db mice were 
significantly increased compared to with wild-type controlWT mice while HDL-C 
level presented a notable decrease. After 4 weeks of niazirin treatment, significant 
decrease was noted in levels of LDL-C, TG and NEFA, whereas higher dose of 
niazirin also reduce the level of TC (p < 0.05). Significant increase was observed in 
plasma HDL-C with niazirin administration (p < 0.01). Collectively, these data 
proved that niazirin can could improve lipid metabolism disorder in db/db mice.


13
3.7 Niazirin relieved NAFLD in db/db （H&E）
Based on the potent effective regulation of niazirin on lipid homeostasis, we test its 
effect on NAFLD (Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease), which is a clinical pathological 
syndrome caused by non-alcoholic and non-specific hepatic damage factors and 
characterized by excessive lipogenesis in liver cells, also considered as the 
manifestation of metabolic syndrome in the liver (Haas, Francque, & Staelset al., 
2016). In order to observe the protective effects of niazirin on the liver tissue structure 
of db/db mice, we examined the histological examination of liver sections (Figure 5A). 
Compared to the normal miceWT group, the hepatocyte of db/db mice was markedly 
swelled, numerous different sizes of round fat droplets were filled in the cytoplasm, 
and infiltration of inflammatory cell and disordered arrangement of liver cells were 
also can be observed, which indicates that the liver tissue has been severely impaired, 
leading to serious NAFLD. However, after 4 weeks niazirin treated, the swelling of 
liver cells was relieved, the accumulation of lipid in the liver was inhibited, 
inflammatory cells were decreased, and the structure of hepatocytes were restored. 
Histology score analysis for NAFLD activity showed that niazirin significantly 
improved liver histology in db/db (Figure 5 B). Meanwhile, in order to detect the lipid 
deposition in the liver of mice, we quantified the lipid profile area percentage by 
Image J (Figure 5 C). We found that the lipid profile area percentage in the liver of 
mice in the DM group was up to 50%, which means that the db/db mice have got 
severe NAFLD, while the lipid profile area percentage of the liver of mice in the DM 
+ 10 and DM + 20 groups was significantly reduced, indicating that the treatment of 
niazirin significantly improved NAFLD in db/db mice. In addition, cCompared with 
wild-type mice, organ coefficient of liver increased significantly in db/db mice, while 


14
organ coefficient of liver was remarkably decreased in niazirin-treatedDM+10 and 
DM+20  groups in a dose-dependent manner, suggesting that swelling symptoms 
were relieved (Figure 5 DB). These results showed that niazirin has could repair 
effects onthe liver steatosis and NAFLD. 
3.8 Niazirin reduced fatty acid synthesis and induced fatty acid oxidation in liver of 
db/db mice
The strong hypolipidemic effect of niazirin in db/db mice prompted us to 
investigate the changes caused by niazirin in hepatic lipid metabolism. Activated 
AMPK (THR172 of AMPK's α-subunit is phosphorylated) regulates hepatic lipid 
metabolism by regulating several transcription factors, such as Peroxisome 
proliferator-activated receptor alpha (PPARα) and Sterol regulatory element-binding 
protein (SREBP-1), which control the expression of fatty acid metabolic enzymes 
(Guo & Choung, 2017; Liu, Zhong, Yin, & Jiang,et al., 2017). We found that 
supplementation of niazirin dose-dependently increased the AMPK phosphorylation 
(Figure 6 A). The main regulatory protein involved in fatty acid β-oxidation of the 
liver, PPARα, was showed highermore expressioned in WT mice than the DM mice, 
while tended to be increase slightly after treating with niazirin. 
As an important transcription regulator of lipid metabolism in the liver, SREBP-1 
regulates the transcription of FAS and ACC, VLDL assembly and intracellular fatty 
acid transport, participates in fatty acid biosynthesis. The expression of SREBP-1 in 
normal group mice was low, while the expression of SREBP-1 was significantly 
increased in db/db mice. Treatment of niazirin caused the reduction of SREBP-1 
expression in db/db mice (Figure 6B). We also measured the activity of FAS, which is 
a rate-limiting enzyme for of fatty acid synthesis and also an effective inhibitor of 


15
fatty acid oxidation (Moritz Hunkeler, 2018). FAS expression tended to increase in 
db/db mice compared to the wild-typeWT mice, which can explain the excessive fatty 
acid synthesis in db/db mice (Figure 6B). Niazirin treatment reduced the expression of 
FAS in the liver of db/db mice in a dose-dependent manner, indicating that niazirin 
can reduce the hepatic fatty acid synthesis. 
ACC, a functional enzyme system that catalyzes the carboxylation of acetyl 
coenzyme A into malonyl coenzyme A. Meanwhile, AMPK is the main kinase 
regulator of ACC and phosphorylates many serine residues on ACC (Park et al., 
2002), phosphor-ACC is also a marker of AMPK activity. Phosphorylation of ACC 
can inhibit its activity and thus inhibit the synthesis of hepatic fatty acids, improves 
insulin sensitivity and may have an optimistic effect on the incidence of obesity, 
diabetes and NAFLD (non-alcohol fatty liver disease) (Harriman, Greenwood, Bhat, 
Huang, Wang, Paul, et al., 2016). The expression of ACC and phosphorylated ACC in 
the liver of db/db mice was abnormal compared with the WT group, and the treatment 
of niazirin repaired the expression to normal level, thus regulating the synthesis of 
fatty acids in the liver (Figure 6C). These results shown that niazirin can correct the 
imbalance of fatty acid metabolism in the liver, keeping hepatic lipid homeostasis 
under control. 
4 Discussion
In our current study, the important phenomena were that niazirin could improve 
insulin resistance, hyperglycemia, hyperlipidemia and NAFLD. These significant 
effects of niazirin were mediated by the reduction of gluconeogenesis and lipid 
accumulation, as well as by the improvement of glycolysis and lipid oxidation. With 
further study on the mechanism of niazirin, we focused on AMPK, which is a key 


16
energy regulator in liver. The novelty of our study was that we find the therapeutic 
effect of niazirin on metabolic syndrome, meanwhile, we explained that niazirin kept 
energy homeostasis via the activation of AMPK signal pathway.
Over the past years, as most patients developed side effects to drug treatments for 
metabolic syndrome over time, a combination treatment strategy, including additional 
drug or insulin administration is often used (Chen, Du, Li, Ma, Geng, Yao, et al., 
2017). Moringa oleifera Lam., as an edible plant, contains not only nutrients but also 
bioactive components such as alkaloids, sterols, glucosinolates, isothiocyanates, 
phenolic glycosides and flavonoids, has always been used as an auxiliary treatment 
for metabolic syndrome (Förster, Ulrichs, Schreiner, Müller, & Mewiet al.s, 2015; 
Joung, Kim, Park, Lee, Kim, Sim, et al., 2017; Matshediso, Cukrowska, & Chimukaet 
al., 2015; Omodanisi, et alAboua, & Oguntibeju, 2017). Therefore, we isolated and 
identified a phenolic glycoside from the seed of Moringa oleifera Lam. that 
ameliorates metabolic syndrome in db/db mice.
Biosynthesis of glycogen and lipid is the main means for the body to store 
excessive nutrients and is strictly regulated by a complex network of hormones and 
metabolic signals (Lin et al., 2016). However, insulin resistance transfers the major 
form of hepatic energy storage from glycogen to TG (Kusunoki et al., 2002). Such 
energy storage mechanisms increase fatty acid and cholesterol synthesis, and reduce 
fatty acid β-oxidation. Ultimately may lead to pancreatic β-cell dysfunction and 
metabolic syndrome (Bardini et al., 2011). Therefore, the main cause of metabolic 
syndrome is insulin resistance and abnormal glucose and lipid metabolism. Since 
db/db mice show obesity at an early stage due to the lack of leptin receptor, which 
increases the risk of insulin resistance thus aggravates the condition of diabetes (Belke 


17
& Severson, 2012). In this study, 5 weeks age db /db mice was used as a typical 
model of obese T2DM with obvious characteristics of metabolic syndrome. Based on 
our previous studies, Moringa oleifera Lam. could improve insulin resistance and 
glucose metabolism in HepG2 cells. Herein, we found that niazirin, a phenolic 
glycoside isolated from the seed of Moringa oleifera Lam. could adjust physiological 
indexes of db/db mice to a normal range, such as the reduction of food intake, water 
intake and body weight, reducinge the blood glucose level and improving 
inflammation. We illustrated the improvement of niazirin on metabolic syndrome of 
db/db mice from the perspective of insulin resistance, hepatic carbohydrates and lipid 
metabolism. 
Liver is the center of carbohydrates metabolism in the body, when the insulin 
sensitivity starts to decrease, insulin resistance will first occur in liver, thus affect the 
enzyme activity related to carbohydrates metabolism, reduce the ability of liver cells 
to decompose and utilize glucose and synthesis glycogen, and increase the liver 
gluconeogenesis to release more glucose into the blood (Jimba, Nakagami, Takahashi, 
Wakamatsu, Hirota, Iwamoto, et al., 2010). Our results showed that niazirin could 
restore the form of energy storage to glycogen in the liver of db/db mice, which 
indicated that niazirin could adjusted hepatic glucose homeostasis. Moreover, we 
observed that the activity of PK and HK were elevated and the activity of G6Pase and 
PEPCK were suppressed by niazirin, thus suppressed gluconeogenesis and , promoted 
glycolysis and liver carbohydrates metabolism, ameliorated metabolic syndrome. 
Other studies have reported that the expression of PEPCK and G6Pase were mediated 
by HNF-4α and FOXO1, which were suppressed by AMPK (Yi, Renaud, Danica, 
Susan, Kim, Simon, et al., 2008). Genetic and pharmacological studies also shown 


18
that AMPK is essential for the maintenance of glucose homeostasis (Bei, Gaochao, & 
Caiet al., 2009). Therefore, we assumed that niazirin may might act as AMPK agonist 
and reduce hepatic gluconeogenesis. Above results forced us to think about the 
possible mechanism by which niazirin improved hepatic carbohydrates metabolism 
was AMPK-mediated.
It is well known that AMPK couldan regulate carbohydrate metabolism and energy 
balance (Ke, Xu, Li, Luo, & Huanget al., 2018; Yin, Kim, Nyachoti, Yao, Li, Tian, et 
al., 2017). AMPK couldan be activated by the phosphorylation of its α-subunit, and 
then regulates its downstream targets, such as SirT1 and PFKFB3, finally improves 
the metabolism of glucose. Therefore, we hypothesized that AMPK was the likely to 
be the possible target of niazirin. As expected, niazirin increased the phosphorylation 
of AMPKα and the expression of PFKFB3 in the liver of db/db mice. The ressults 
suggested that niazirin activated AMPK to regulate carbohydrate metabolism in liver. 
Furthermore, previous studies showed that the phosphorylation of AMPKα could 
activate SirT1, and SirT1 could interact with PGC-1α and deacetylate it (Ghiraldini, 
Crispim, & Melloet al., 2013; Wu, Deng, Shi, Su, Wei, & Duanet al., 2016). Thus, we 
explored the expression of SirT1 and PGC-1α in liver. Consistent with previous 
studies (Zang, et al.Fan, Chen, Huang, & Qin, 2018), in the conditions of abnormal 
energy metabolism, the expression of SirT1 in db/db mice was lower than normal WT 
group, while the expression of PGC-1α was higher than normal group. However, after 
treated by niazirin, the expression of SirT1 and PGC-1α were almost adjusted to 
normal levels. In addition, PGC-1α is the coactivator of HNF-4α and FOXO1, which 
control the expression of gluconeogenic enzymes PEPCK and G6Pase, respectively 
(Sharabi, et al., 2017). Our study found that niazirin downregulated the expression of 


19
HNF-4α and FOXO1, which indicated that niazirin could inhibited the excessive 
gluconeogenesis in db/db mice. We therefore demonstrated that niazirin could 
increase the phosphorylation of AMPK then regulate its downstream targets to 
improve hepatic carbohydrate metabolism in db/db mice.
Meanwhile, insulin resistance caused by metabolic syndrome can could also be 
attributed to the high secretion of TNF-α and low secretion of IL-10 (Forbes & 
Cooper, 2013; Olson, Callas, Hanley, Andreas, Haffner, Wagenknecht, et al., 2012). 
Excessive or insufficient secretion of cytokines such as IL-10 and TNF-α intensified 
insulin resistance in db/db mice, leading to an insensitive of adipocytes to insulin. 
Such conditions may cause lipotoxicity and inhibite the ability of insulin to stimulate 
the cells' absorptivity of NEFA which produced by the circulation of TG lipolysis and 
caused inhibition lipolysis of endogenous TG to NEFA (Yazıcı & Sezer, 2017). 
Meanwhile, excess plasma NEFA impairs cellular insulin secretion, suppresses liver 
glycogenesis and inhibits skeletal muscle glucose processing, thus aggravates 
hyperglycemia (Mbikay, 2012). However, after 4 weeks of niazirin treatment, the 
levels of proinflammatory cytokines in db/db mice were decreased, insulin resistance 
and hyperglycemia were alleviated, lipotoxicity was reduced and lipid metabolism 
returned to normal. Since the increase of free fatty acids flow, decrease of triglyceride 
clearance and limitation of fatty acids oxidation may result in increased fatty acid 
synthesis. These changes in lipid metabolism may lead to the occurrence of NAFLD 
(Shiffman & Gunn, 2017), while niazirin alleviated dyslipidemia, which promoting us 
to explore if niazirin could improve NAFLD. In line with previous observation 
(Williamson, 2015), severe NAFLD were observed in db/db mice. Surprisingly, 
niazirin had therapeutic effects on NAFLD of db/db mice. The imbalance of fatty acid 


20
synthesis and oxidation couldan lead to excessive accumulation of lipids in the liver 
and increase the susceptibility to NAFLD (Gross, Pawlak, Lefebvre, & Staelset al., 
2017), which is the result of the interaction of various factors. In this study, we 
focused on the regulatory effect of niazirin on hepatic lipid metabolism. 
As AMPK is the upstream regulator of genes related to lipid metabolism, such as 
fatty acid synthesis and oxidation. In this study, we found that niazirin increased 
phosphorylation of AMPK. Therefore, we hypothesized that AMPK was likely to be 
targeted by niazirin to regulate hepatic lipid metabolism. Furthermore, AMPK 
regulates fatty acid synthesis and fatty acid oxidation mediated by SREBP-1. The 
inhibited SREBP-1 reduced the expression of ACC and FAS at the transcription level. 
Meanwhile, activated AMPK phosphorylated and inactivated ACC lead to the 
inhibition of synthesis of fatty acids and cholesterol and which then increase fatty acid 
oxidation (Garcia & Shaw, 2017). The present study showed that phospho-ACC 
significantly decreased in db/db mice, indicating that the activity of AMPK in db/db 
mice was inhibited. Meanwhile, the levels of SREBP-1 target protein FAS and ACC 
were increased, resulting in increased fatty acid synthesis and decreased fatty acid 
oxidation. However, we found that the inactivation of SREBP-1, FAS and ACC was 
increased by niazirin. In addition, the expression of SREBP-1 in liver is activated by 
insulin (Tang, Wu, Tang, Ge, Wang, Hong, et al., 2017), thus in the animal models of 
obesity and T2D, the overexpression of liver SREBP-1 has been proved to be related 
to hyperlipidemia (Liu, Zhong, Yin, & Jianget al., 2017). Therefore, niazirin may also 
inhibited the overexpression of SREBP-1 by decreasing the insulin level in db/db 
mice. PPARα controls lipid flux in the liver by regulating fatty acid transport and 
β-oxidation as well as keeping plasma lipid profiles by taking fatty acids and various 


21
fatty acid derivative compounds as endogenous ligands (Kersten, 2014; Takei, Han, 
Murayama, Satoh, Oikawa, Ohno, et al., 2017). Moreover, deficiency of PPARα 
increases susceptibility to NAFLD and hepatic inflammation (Ge, Yu, Xu, Li, Fan, Li, 
et al., 2016). In this study, we found that niazirin dose-dependently upregulated 
PPARα, thus enhanced lipid oxidation, regulated plasma lipid profiles and 
ameliorated NAFLD. In aggregate, activation of AMPK by niazirin in liver leading to 
a series of beneficial metabolic effects, indicating that niazirin is expected to 
ameliorate metabolic syndrome (Figure S1).
In conclusion, this study reported that niazirin plays a certain role in the control of 
metabolic syndrome in db/db mice, such as inflammation, insulin resistance, 
hyperglycemia, hyperlipidemia, and NAFLD. In addition, niazirin improved hepatic 
energy metabolism thereby ameliorating metabolic syndrome, which may be 
associated with the activation of AMPK pathway. Since niazirin is a phenolic 
glycoside from Moringa oleifera Lam. seed, which has long been used as an edible 
plant, the outcome of our study suggested an effective food-assist therapeutic 
approach for treatment of metabolic syndrome. We proposed that better understanding 
of niazirin could open up possibilities to maintain energy homeostasis in patients with 
metabolic syndrome with dietary supplementation.
